sources.title: Censoring of outcomes and regressors due to survey nonresponse: Identification and estimation using weights and imputations

sources.title: Cell lineage statistics with incomplete population trees
sources.inspected: Primary author manuscript sections II-III, empirical application, growth bounds and Discussion
sources.known: Forward lineage weights, inclusion of terminated paths, and bounds on growth. Broad termination includes known removal as well as death.
sources.relation: Growth bounds differ from biological survival bounds for an unseen daughter. Unknown biological fate cannot be coded as death merely from disappearance.

sources.title: Lineage EM algorithm for inferring latent states from cellular lineage trees
sources.inspected: Primary author manuscript introduction, Figure 4 and sections 3.1-3.3
sources.known: Chronological random paths, retrospective survivor ancestry, tree samples and pruning differ; latent-state estimation accounts for sampling bias.
sources.relation: Observation-rule distinctions and pruning concerns are known; no exact missing-branch family-selected envelope located.

sources.relation: Direct prior recognition of information gap; does not establish novelty or biological identification of this proposal.

finite_record_target.R: Fixed recorded baseline roster; not presumed complete original cohort
finite_record_target.u: Random forward-daughter survival probability, with tag remaining dead after death
finite_record_target.denominator: Require at least one included family; retain feasibility of zero denominator separately
finite_record_target.weights: 2^(-g), where g counts divisions after chosen baseline; do not renormalize missing-daughter mass onto observed sister
finite_record_target.distinction: Path weights are not probabilities of inclusion in original source recording

bound_review.outer_not_tree_sharp: Independent interval/status optimization may be sharp for its relaxation but is only an outer bound for coupled tree completions
necessary_couplings: Positive endpoint family survival gives positive endpoint tag weight in finite resolved tree; zero can be unattained infimum with unrestricted hidden depth
Unknown identity/timing/mask assignments must be included in completion scope
bound_review.contrasts: Marginal subtraction is conservative and generally nonsharp; zero in every separate contrast does not certify one joint equality-producing completion
bound_review.empty_set: No compatible completion may reflect graph/timing inconsistency, not a biological effect
bound_review.complete_case_illustration: With B required links independently observed with probability p, P(complete|B)=p^B, so constant local tracking errors still select by branch opportunity count. Analytic illustration, not fitted.

population_boundary.known_coverage_example: If recorded conditional population mean is bounded by [L,U] and pi_T known, support [0,1] yields [pi_T*L, pi_T*U+1-pi_T]. This is not computed for the data.
population_boundary.unknown_coverage: When original denominator and family-survivor-specific coverage are unrestricted, population bounds generally reduce to [0,1] in closure
population_boundary.warning: The finite-record envelope does not automatically bound the recorded conditional population mean; total recording fraction is not family-survivor coverage

sampling_boundary.statement: Identification/completion envelopes are not confidence intervals. Finite cohorts under population horizon invariance can have unequal empirical curves.
sampling_boundary.contrast_excludes_zero: A fixed-record contrast envelope excluding zero establishes a sign for that empirical contrast under the completion relaxation; alone it does not reject the stochastic null.
requirements_for_population_test: Sampling uncertainty distinct from missing-data ambiguity
Applicable inferential method; no confidence procedure selected here
